# Use Claude to Rewrite an Angry Email So It Says What You Actually Mean

> **In short:** Paste your angry draft into Claude, add one line about who you're writing to, and it returns a calmer version that keeps your real point. Free with a Claude.ai account; works on phone and desktop in any browser.

You've just typed something you'd never actually send — full of sarcasm, CAPS, and three exclamation marks. Before you regret hitting send, Claude can reshape that draft in seconds: same meaning, fewer grenades. This guide walks you through the five-minute version, and one honest thing to know up front — Claude drafts the email for you, but it cannot send it from your account. You still copy, paste, and press send yourself.

## Before you start

- **A free Claude account.** Sign up at claude.ai with your email or Google account if you don't have one. The free tier covers everything in this guide.
- **Your angry draft somewhere you can copy it.** A Notes app, a Gmail draft, even a screenshot works — you'll paste it into Claude in Step 2.
- **Roughly 5 minutes.** Most of that is reading Claude's rewrite and tweaking one or two lines.
- **An honest read of what you actually want.** "I want them to fix the bug by Friday" is much more useful to Claude than "I'm furious." We'll cover this in Step 3.

## Step 1 — Open a fresh chat in Claude

Go to **claude.ai** in any browser, or open the Claude mobile app, and sign in. Look for a button labeled **"New chat"** or **"Start chat"** — usually at the top of the sidebar on desktop, or as a **+** icon at the top of the conversation list on mobile. Click it. A blank conversation appears with a small text field at the bottom and a paperclip icon for attachments. Starting fresh matters: if you reuse an old chat, Claude may carry over context from a previous task, and your email rewrite will land in the wrong tone. If you can't find the new-chat button, look for a **pencil icon**, a **"+"**, or your account avatar in the corner — apps rearrange these often. 💬 Example: type "Hi" and press Enter once, just to confirm the chat is working. You'll know it worked when you see an empty conversation with no previous messages and a blinking cursor in the message box.

## Step 2 — Paste your angry draft as the first message

Click into the message box at the bottom of the screen and paste your full draft — yes, even the CAPS and the sarcastic bits. Claude isn't judging you; it's reading the rough emotion so it knows what to soften. After you paste, the text fills the box; if it's longer than the visible area, the box will grow or scroll. Press **Enter** (or tap the **send** arrow ➤ on mobile) to submit. Claude reads it and replies within a few seconds, with its first attempt at a rewrite. If your draft is in a screenshot, look for a **paperclip or camera icon** next to the message box — tap it, pick the image, and add a short note saying "rewrite this email". On desktop, the same paperclip lets you upload files. You'll know it worked when Claude responds with a rewritten version of your email, not a question or an apology.

## Step 3 — Tell Claude who you're writing to and what you actually want

Claude's first rewrite is usually a safe, polite version. The next message is where you steer it. In the same chat, type two short pieces of information: **who the reader is** (your boss, a vendor, a coworker, your landlord) and **the one outcome you want** (a refund, an apology, a deadline moved, a meeting booked). Press Enter. Watch what Claude does: it reads your follow-up, adjusts the tone, and gives you a second version. Often the second version is the one you'll actually send. If the tone didn't shift between version one and version two, your follow-up was too vague — try again with more detail about the reader. 💬 Example: "This is going to my project manager. I want them to move the deadline from Friday to next Wednesday because the design files aren't ready. Keep it short — under 120 words." You'll know it worked when the new version names the right person, includes your specific ask, and reads like something you'd actually type yourself.

## Step 4 — Ask for tone tweaks without starting over

This is where the back-and-forth pays off. If the rewrite is still too cold, too formal, or accidentally passive-aggressive, tell Claude in plain words what feels off. Type something like "softer, please" or "more direct, less apology" or "remove the line about 'understanding their busy schedule' — it sounds sarcastic." Claude rewrites again, keeping the structure and adjusting only the part you flagged. On screen, you'll see a new version appear below your last message, with the older ones still visible above. If the rewrite gets worse, look for a **"Retry"** or **"Regenerate"** button near Claude's response — usually a small circular arrow — to get a fresh attempt without losing your instructions. If you can't find a retry button, just type "try again" in the chat; it has the same effect. 💬 Example: "Drop the apology paragraph. I don't need to apologize — I need the refund processed by Monday." You'll know it worked when the new version reads like something a calm, confident version of you would write, and you'd be comfortable seeing it in your sent folder.

## Step 5 — Copy the final version and send it yourself

When you have a version you like, click and drag to select the rewritten email, then copy it with **Ctrl+C** (Windows) or **Cmd+C** (Mac), or long-press on mobile and choose **Copy**. Open your email app — Gmail, Outlook, Apple Mail, whatever you use — paste it into a new message, fill in the recipient and subject line, and send as you normally would. Claude drafts; you deliver. If you're not ready to send yet, save the draft and sleep on it; sending angry emails the next morning is rarely a regret. On screen, you'll see Claude's full reply in the chat, but you only need the email body — ignore any intro lines Claude adds like "Here's a rewritten version:" and copy only the actual email text. You'll know it worked when the email is sitting in your outbox (or drafts folder) in your own account, addressed to the right person, and your hands feel calmer than they did ten minutes ago.

## Common mistakes

- **Letting Claude send the email for you.** It can't. Claude is a chat tool — it drafts the message, but you copy, paste, and hit send from your own email app. Anything claiming to "send automatically" is a different tool, not Claude.
- **Skipping the "what do I actually want" line.** A rewrite without context is a generic polite version. Always tell Claude the reader and the outcome, or you'll get a draft that's pleasant but doesn't move anything forward.
- **Forgetting to remove the worst lines.** Claude sometimes leaves one sarcastic phrase behind because it appeared in your original. Read the final version once more before you copy — if a line makes you wince, ask Claude to cut it.
- **Sending the first rewrite without checking.** The first response is a starting point, not a finished email. The second or third version, after you've given feedback, is almost always the one worth sending.

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life:** The next time a customer service reply makes your eye twitch, or a note from a neighbor pushes a button, you can draft a response in two minutes instead of stewing for an hour — and the message you actually send will be the calm one.
- **For your business or work:** Most professional conflict gets worse because of tone, not content. A 30-second Claude pass before sending a frustrated email to a client, vendor, or coworker turns a relationship risk into a routine message.
- **If you're just getting started:** Don't wait for a big blow-up. Practice once this week on a low-stakes email that bugged you — a slow refund, a missed meeting — so the workflow is familiar the next time something bigger lands.

## Try it now

Find one email you wrote this week that felt a little sharper than you wanted. Paste it into Claude, add one line about who it's going to and what you want, and ask for a calmer rewrite. Then send the new version (or save it as a draft). Two minutes, one less regret.
